issues.description: Tests fabricate a zero-amount, zero-puzzle-hash Addition to bypass the non-empty additions invariant.
issues.detail: Tests changed `additions=[]` to `additions=[Addition(amount=uint64(0), puzzle_hash=bytes32.zeros)]` to satisfy `len(self.additions) < 1`. A sentinel addition is value-as-flag and silently mutates the postcondition. Either CreateSignedTransaction should allow empty additions, or the test was edited to fit the new code rather than the spec. State the invariant and fix one side.

issues.description: CreateSignedTransaction now complects XCH-send, CAT-spend, and signed-tx-creation into one record with no mutual-exclusivity validation.
issues.detail: Adding extra_delta, tail_reveal, tail_solution, and puzzle_decorator as first-class fields admits nonsensical states (e.g., XCH send with tail_reveal set). Valid field combinations are unstated and unenforced. Add a __post_init__ invariant or decompose into a shared core function over a small sum of explicit request values.

issues.description: cat_discrepancy_validation uses opaque `None in {a, b, c}` set-membership with type-ignore suppressions.
issues.detail: The tri-state validation relies on set-construction semantics over mixed types and requires `# type: ignore[arg-type]` to narrow. A proper CatDiscrepancy value type constructed at the boundary, or `any(x is None for x in (...))` with a TypeGuard, would state the invariant explicitly and remove the ignores rather than duplicating them by extraction.

issues.description: get_wallet is called purely for its raising side effect, labelled only by a `# opportunity to raise` comment.
issues.detail: The discarded call smuggles a precondition assertion via folklore rather than structure. A named guard like `_assert_wallet_type(wallet_id, Wallet)` would make the contract explicit and prevent a future reader from deleting the apparently-dead line.

issues.description: send_transaction silently drops `puzzle_decorator[0]`-only slicing; cat_spend drops the per-addition MAX_COIN_AMOUNT check.
issues.detail: Old code passed `[request.puzzle_decorator[0].to_json_dict()]` — exactly one decorator — and explicitly raised on additions exceeding MAX_COIN_AMOUNT. The new path forwards the whole list and assumes create_signed_transaction enforces the bound. Either the downstream invariants match (cite them) or observable behavior has changed silently.

issues.description: Memos encoding boundary and JSON round-tripping through transport for in-process callers are incidental complexity.
issues.detail: Old send_transaction passed `memos=[[mem.encode("utf-8") ...]]` (bytes); new path wraps list[str] into Addition.memos with unclear downstream encoding. Both callers also serialize a typed value via json_serialize_for_transport only to have a sibling method deserialize it. Factor a shared core function over values and audit the memos encoding contract.

synthesis.summary: The deduplication intent is sound, but the chosen shape complects three distinct request types into one CreateSignedTransaction without stating which field combinations are valid, and the diff silently changes observable behavior in at least two places (puzzle_decorator slicing, MAX_COIN_AMOUNT enforcement). The clearest tell is the test edit that fabricates a zero-amount, zero-puzzle Addition to bypass the non-empty-additions invariant — the test was bent to fit the code rather than the contract. The cat_discrepancy tri-state validation and `# opportunity to raise` pattern smuggle invariants via folklore and type-ignores instead of named structure. Refactor is valuable but author must state equivalence claims, lift CatDiscrepancy to a value type, and add explicit guards before merge.
